assumptions: Read length and dead zone are the facility's published figures, or the ones given.
limits: Reports the coverage the walk achieves and any stretch it cannot reach rather than claiming full coverage.
Each primer is the graded pair designer's; what this adds is the walk, whose coverage the test re-derives by a second algorithm.
bio.jane/contract.question: Which walk of primers reads this whole region, with what overlap, and what cannot be reached?

description: Design a WALK of sequencing primers that reads a whole region, not one pair: tiled reads with confirmed overlap, on both strands by default, plus the coverage the walk actually achieves and any stretch it cannot reach. This is the 'how do I read all 6 kb of this construct' question, which a single pair does not answer. Read length and dead zone default to a named facility's published figures (MSU RTSF, ABI 3730XL) rather than to round numbers.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

both_strands.description: read every base from both directions - what a sequencing facility means by double-stranded coverage, and the standard for anything deposited or published.

dead_zone.description: bases at the start of a read that are not trustworthy. Default 35 is the LONGEST the same source warns about (it says the first 25-35 bases are poor), so an untouched walk is the cautious reading in both directions. In bp. Advanced.

min_length.description: shortest acceptable primer. In bp. Advanced.

overlap.description: confirmed overlap required between consecutive reads on one strand. Overlap is what turns abutting reads into a contig. Default 100 has NO published source and is a judgement, which is why it is stated rather than dressed as a figure. In bp.

read_length.description: usable bases per read, AFTER the dead zone. Default 800 is the shortest read MSU RTSF Genomics Core, Sanger Sequencing Best and Worst Practices (2024-04-25), ABI 3730XL promises (it quotes 800-900), which is the cautious end of a published range rather than a round number. In bp.

region_end.description: 0-based inclusive end of the region to read. Unset = the whole template. Advanced.

region_start.description: 0-based inclusive start of the region to read. Unset = the whole template. Advanced.

target_tm.description: target melting temperature for each primer in the walk. In °C. Advanced.

name: design_sequencing_primers

authority.description: the published source the read-length and dead-zone defaults come from

complete.description: true when every base of the region is read at least once

coverage.description: every stretch of the region, contiguous and in order, with its depth

doubleStranded.description: true when every base is read from both directions

gaps.description: stretches no read reaches - empty means the region is fully read

primers.description: just the primer sequences, in walk order, for ordering

readCount.description: how many primers the walk needs

reads.description: one entry per primer in the walk: name (F1, R1, ...), sequence, strand, and the stretch it is expected to read

singleStranded.description: stretches read from one strand only, when both were asked for

skipped.description: anchors where no primer could be designed, each with the reason - never a silently short walk

used.description: the parameters the plan was actually built under, so a readout never restates them
